highlights.text: one core idea: extension or stretching out, in either space or time
named from this root because a mountain "extends" in length and breadth
"he did it stage after stage,"
b-n-y as one root meaning to build or construct
"I built the building, I build it"
the line of Imruʾ al-Qays: "…not built close upon its string."
One sound, regular root: pushing something forward.
dafaqa al-māʾ — water gushed forth; māʾ dāfiq — gushing water
one root meaning (aṣl wāḥid): a thing's entering under concealment and secrecy
"I thrust the thing into the earth"
thrust it (yadussuhu) into the dust?"
a single core idea: an increase or excess in something
surplus, extra — and, by extension
claims superiority over his equals and peers
Imruʾ al-Qays describing a woman who sleeps late
a sound root (aṣl ṣaḥīḥ) indicating an opening up and a parting (tafattuḥ, infirāj)
Fakāk al-rahn is the release of a pledge
lā yazālu, "he keeps on doing that."
a single sound root whose core sense is roundness or circularity in a thing
The celestial sphere / orbit (فَلَكُ السَّمَاء)
The ship, فُلْك
a single core sense: gentleness/deliberateness and stillness or quiet
Ibn Fāris takes it from hāda / yahūdu, "to repent, turn back," the verbal noun being hawd.
a single core meaning: to pour or tip out something measurable, letting it flow out freely
the passive participle mahīl (مَهِيل, "poured/tipped out")
one root meaning the gathering of a thing and coming-together
"I collected the wealth"
a basin or cistern is called جَابِيَة (jābiya)
likened to "the cistern of the Iraqi elder, brimming over."
One core meaning: the smallness/scantiness of what is drunk (a sip).
jariʿa al-shāribu al-māʾ / jaraʿa yajraʿu — to sip water
"aflata fulānun bi-jurayʿati al-dhaqan"
highlights.note: saying of the Arabs, via al-Farrāʾ

highlights.text: a single core meaning: **swerving or deviation from the road**
jāra, jawran = "to deviate from the way."
"Do not give it to drink the downpour of a rumbling, roaring [cloud]."
one single underlying idea: al-lajaʾ / al-malja' — "the place one takes refuge in."
Winter has come, and I had not yet made myself a lajaʾ [refuge/shelter]
a single, coherent root whose core sense is: taking food by hand to the mouth
both mean "I took it in / swallowed it [as a mouthful]."
One core meaning: extension in a thing, and stretching-out.
illustrated with a line of poetry by Imruʾ al-Qays about driving mounts until exhausted, even outrunning the need for reins
a single sound root whose core notion is a tearing or rending in something
the doubled (intensive) form مَزَّقَ / يُمَزِّقُ
"I tore the people apart," i.e. scattered them
the root n-h-j carries two separate, unrelated core meanings
al-manhaj = also "road, path"; plural al-manahij.
a single sound root whose core idea is undoing something that had been made or bound
nakatha al-ʿahd, yankuthu
"Whenever there is a matter of the nakītha, I am present."
taking/picking fruit off a tree.
Noun qiṭf = a cluster or bunch (e.g. of grapes).
"but your patron's face scratches" (walākinna wajha mawlāka taqṭifu)
a person's cucumber-patch is his مقثأة (maqthaʾa)
a single root, all of it bound to the number three
Its base sense is the numeral three, as in اثنان وثلاثة (two and three).
the image al-Shammākh had in mind in a cited line
one core meaning: khushūʿ — humble, lowly submission
akhbata yukhbitu ikhbātan means "he showed khushūʿ"
the Qur'anic word al-mukhbitīn — "those who are humbly submissive"
Khardal — classed by the ʿAyn as a kind of ḥarf-plant
describing someone feeding two lions dust-covered pieces of meat cut this way
a single root meaning to keep something safe, to guard or store it
"I stored away the dirham and the like"
"its meat is not stored up among us; only the hoarder's meat is stored"
making a thing firm and secure
writing and reading
a lump or piece of iron; plural زُبَر
I wrote the document; from this comes الزَّبُور
a line by Ibn Aḥmar
